description: Mechanical verification registry for this workspace. Each entry names a file and a pattern, and says whether that pattern is expected to be present or absent; scripts/verify_issues.py decides whether the claim still holds. Identifiers are local to this repository and do not correspond to identifiers in any other one. A pattern is matched line by line with Python's re, so it must match within a single line: a string spanning adjacent source literals that the interpreter joins cannot be pinned, because no line contains it.

issues.title: Stream cancellation refuses the string request IDs JSON-RPC permits
issues.description: _handle_mgp_cancel accepts params.request_id only when it is an int and answers invalid-params otherwise. JSON-RPC 2.0 defines an id as a String, Number or NULL, and this package's own helpers already type request ids as int or str: write_mgp_method_response and write_mgp_stream_chunk both accept either. The gap handler repeats the same integer-only test. A client that follows the specification and numbers its requests with strings can therefore never cancel a stream -- the cancel is answered as malformed even while a stream is registered under that exact id, so the stream runs to completion and the client is told it asked wrongly.
issues.measured: _handle_mgp_cancel driven with request_id 'req-abc' while the active-stream map held that key: the reply was error -32602 'params.request_id must be an integer', and the registered stream was never signalled.

issues.title: Servers advertise the streaming extension while streaming is disabled
issues.description: _build_mgp_capabilities declares the streaming extension unconditionally, but ProviderConfig.supports_streaming defaults to False and the call handler enters the streaming path only when that flag is true. The declaration is what a peer negotiates on, so a peer reading it asks for chunks this server will never emit. The declaration should follow the flag it claims to describe.
issues.measured: A ProviderConfig with supports_streaming False produced extensions ['permissions', 'streaming'].

issues.title: A malformed stream line is discarded and the answer is still reported complete
issues.description: The event-stream reader catches a JSON decode error on a data line and continues, so a chunk that fails to parse is dropped with nothing recorded. The only condition that marks a response as truncated is the absence of the terminating sentinel, so a stream that loses a line in the middle and then terminates normally is returned as a complete answer. The caller cannot tell a whole reply from one with a hole in it, which is the distinction the completeness guarantee exists to make.
issues.measured: A stream of two good deltas, one unparseable line and the sentinel returned a result containing only the two good deltas, carrying streamed true with chunks_sent 2, with no partial marker and no error.

issues.title: Unparseable tool arguments become an empty argument object
issues.description: parse_chat_think_result decodes a tool call's arguments string and, when the decode fails, substitutes an empty dict and appends the call anyway with no error marker. The caller receives a well-formed tool call whose arguments were invented here. A tool invoked with no arguments can mean something very different from the call the model actually asked for, and nothing downstream can tell the two apart.
issues.measured: A call named 'delete_all' whose arguments string was the unterminated '{"scope": "prod' came back as type tool_calls, name 'delete_all', arguments {}, with no error field on the result.

issues.title: The non-streaming provider path has no receive-size budget
issues.description: call_llm_api issues an ordinary post and then parses the whole body, and the streaming error path reads the body in full before parsing it. Neither declares a content-length ceiling nor counts received bytes, so the peer decides how much memory this process spends.
issues.measured: Against a transport returning a 33.6 MB response the call returned normally with all 33554432 characters intact and a traced peak of 67.1 MB, twice the body, because the raw bytes and the decoded string are live at the same moment. Note the limit of the measurement: the body arrived in one piece, so this establishes that nothing rejects an oversized response, not how a cap would behave against a slow sender.

issues.title: Streaming bounds the retransmit buffer but not the accumulated answer
issues.description: The streaming handler keeps a ring buffer of emitted chunks bounded by _CHUNK_BUFFER_MAX, and that bound is documented. The authoritative result, however, is a single string every text delta is appended to, and it must survive until the stream ends. The loop has no output-byte, token or total-duration budget, and read timeouts measure inactivity between chunks rather than elapsed time, so a peer that keeps emitting small chunks holds the request open and the string grows for as long as it does. The bound that exists is not the one that matters.
issues.measured: With the ring buffer at 100 entries, 4000 deltas accumulated 1024000 characters and a traced peak of 6.2 MB; the documented bound never came into play.

issues.title: Search providers parse the whole upstream body before applying max_results
issues.description: Every provider materialises the complete upstream response before it narrows the result set: the JSON providers parse the whole body and then slice to max_results, and the HTML provider decodes the entire document before extracting entries. max_results bounds what the caller sees, not what this process spends, and a bound applied after parsing is not a bound on the parse.
issues.measured: Against a transport returning a 59.1 MB body of 200000 entries with max_results 3, the call returned 3 results after a traced peak of 173.0 MB -- the body plus the parsed structure.

issues.title: A proxy-only deployment still resolves to a direct external endpoint
issues.description: load_llm_provider_config documents that under proxy-only isolation all outbound HTTP is expected to route through the injected proxy, and it uses that proxy as the default endpoint. An explicit endpoint override still wins, and when the override points outside localhost the loader only logs a warning: it neither refuses the configuration nor rewrites it. The provider then posts agent context straight to that host, leaving the boundary the deployment was built to enforce, with a warning line as the only trace. A warning is the right severity for a misconfiguration; it is not the right severity for silently leaving an isolation boundary.
issues.measured: With the proxy variable set and the endpoint override pointing at an external host, the resolved configuration carried the external URL unchanged.
issues.pattern: if proxy_base and \"127\.0\.0\.1\" not in api_url

issues.title: The semantic cache compares vectors of different widths by truncating to the shorter
issues.description: _dot_product pairs its two operands with zip, which stops at the shorter one, and nothing records or compares the width of a stored vector against the width of a query vector. Embedding width is a property of the model, so any change of model or backend leaves entries of one width being scored against queries of another over whatever prefix they share. The score is then compared against a similarity threshold as though it meant the same thing, and a prefix agreement is enough to clear it. The failure is a cache that answers a question it was never asked.
issues.measured: _dot_product of a 384-dimension unit vector and a 768-dimension unit vector returned 1.0. End to end, an entry stored with a 768-dimension backend was returned as a hit for a semantically unrelated query embedded at 384 dimensions.
issues.pattern: return sum\(x \* y for x, y in zip\(a, b\)\)

issues.title: The semantic cache accepts an embedding response of any size and any width
issues.description: _embed issues an ordinary post, parses the whole JSON body, and takes the first vector, with no response-byte ceiling, no batch-cardinality check and no dimension check. The embedding client in this same package validates its responses; this path does not, so the backend decides how much memory a lookup costs and how wide a cached vector is.
issues.measured: A 28.0 MB response carrying a single 4000000-dimension vector was accepted and cached in full, at a traced peak of 261.5 MB.

issues.title: A non-finite embedding is normalised past the guard and cached
issues.description: _embed computes the vector's norm and divides only when the norm exceeds a small epsilon. A vector containing a non-finite value has a non-finite norm, and every comparison against a non-finite number is false, so the guard is not taken and the values are stored exactly as received. Scoring that entry yields a non-finite similarity, and 'greater than the best so far' is false for it too, so the entry can never win a lookup: it occupies a slot in a bounded cache and can never be returned from it. Nothing between the response and the store rejects the value, and nothing afterwards reports that an entry has become unreachable.
issues.measured: A backend response containing a bare NaN token was accepted by _embed and cached with the value intact; scoring it against a unit vector produced a non-finite similarity, and the subsequent lookup returned no hit.
